<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill is tested for impairment annually on October&#160;31 at the reporting unit level or whenever circumstances occur indicating goodwill might be impaired. The impairment test involves comparing the fair value of each reporting unit to its carrying value, including goodwill. Fair value reflects the price a market participant would be willing to pay in a potential sale of the reporting unit. If the fair value exceeds the carrying value, the Company will conclude that <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001458" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" contextRef="C_0001348036_20181030_20181031" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction> goodwill impairment has occurred. If the carrying value of the reporting unit exceeds its fair value, the Company will recognize an impairment loss in an amount equal to the excess, not to exceed the carrying value. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has three reporting units for goodwill impairment testing consisting of its U.S., European, and Brazilian operations. As part of the Company&#8217;s annual impairment test, a qualitative impairment test was performed </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">107</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000479_dcnt_c12edd1c-e55f-4ca3-aa7f-a433d82c5f57">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">for the Company&#8217;s U.S. reporting unit. The Company concluded it is more likely than not that the fair value of the reporting unit exceeds its carrying value. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A quantitative impairment test was performed for the Company&#8217;s European reporting unit. Upon completion, the fair value of the European reporting unit was in excess of the carrying value. When following a quantitative approach, the Company measures the fair value of its reporting units using a combination of a discounted cash flow approach and the market valuation approach using publicly traded company multiples in similar businesses, which are Level&#160;3 measurements. This analysis requires significant judgments, including estimation of future cash flows, which is dependent on internal forecasts, determination of the Company&#8217;s discount rate, which is risk-adjusted to reflect the specific risk profile of the reporting unit being tested, and determination of revenue multiples, which are based on guideline public company multiples and adjusted for the specific size and risk profile of the reporting unit. The discount rate used in the Company&#8217;s most recent annual impairment test was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001459" name="avlr:WeightedAverageCostOfCapital" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_avlrBrazilianReportingUnitMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="2" scale="-2">25</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001460" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_avlrBrazilianReportingUnitMember_20211231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001461" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_avlrBrazilianReportingUnitMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001462" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_avlrBrazilianReportingUnitMember_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> goodwill associated with the Brazilian reporting unit in 2021, 2020, and 2019.&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160; &#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company had $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001464" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairedAccumulatedImpairmentLoss" contextRef="C_0001348036_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001463" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairedAccumulatedImpairmentLoss" contextRef="C_0001348036_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">17.6</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> million of accumulated goodwill impairment as of December&#160;31, 2021, and 2020, which is associated with the Brazilian reporting unit and was recognized in the years ended December 31, 2017, and 2018. </p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000480" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeasesTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001348036_20210101_20211231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000480_dcnt_a84dc052-72d5-413e-a59e-d817cd476dc3">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">8. Leases</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001465" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseDescription" contextRef="C_0001348036_20210101_20211231">The Company has non-cancelable operating leases primarily for office facilities in the United States, Brazil, Europe, and India that expire through 2029. The remaining operating leases are primarily comprised of leases of vehicles, office equipment, and servers.</ix:nonNumeric> As of December&#160;31, 2021, the leases have remaining terms of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001466">0.2 to 7.8 years</span>, <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001468" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseOptionToExtend" contextRef="C_0001348036_20210101_20211231">some of which include options to extend for up to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001470" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20211231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years</ix:nonNumeric> after the initial term, and <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001471" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseOptionToTerminate" contextRef="C_0001348036_20210101_20211231">some of which include options to terminate within<span style="color:#FF0000;"> </span><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001473" name="avlr:LesseeOperatingLeaseTerminateTerm" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20210101_20211231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">2</ix:nonNumeric> years after the commencement date.</ix:nonNumeric> Options to extend or terminate a lease which are not reasonably certain to be exercised are not included in the lease term or in the lease payments for purposes of determining the operating lease right-of-use asset and operating lease liability. At the time of the TTR Merger, the Company was reasonably certain it would exercise its option to extend its lease in McMinnville, OR and as such, the extension was recognized as part of the operating lease right-of-use asset and operating lease liability for that lease. No other options to extend or terminate a lease were reasonably certain as of December 31, 2021, or 2020. The Company&#8217;s lease agreements do not contain material residual value guarantees, restrictions, or covenants. As of December&#160;31, 2021, the Company does not have any finance leases.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Commitments </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has purchase commitments primarily related to network infrastructure, hosting services, and software licenses that extend up to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001508" name="us-gaap:LongtermPurchaseCommitmentPeriod" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtProductOrServiceAxis_us-gaapLicenseAndServiceMember_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20210101_20211231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">four years</ix:nonNumeric> beyond December&#160;31, 2021. The Company&#8217;s obligation for future payments under these contracts is $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001509" name="us-gaap:PurchaseObligationDueInNextTwelveMonths" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtProductOrServiceAxis_us-gaapLicenseAndServiceMember_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">45.6</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001510" name="us-gaap:PurchaseObligationDueInSecondYear" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtProductOrServiceAxis_us-gaapLicenseAndServiceMember_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">32.2</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001511" name="us-gaap:PurchaseObligationDueInThirdYear" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtProductOrServiceAxis_us-gaapLicenseAndServiceMember_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">26.0</ix:nonFraction> million, and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001512" name="us-gaap:PurchaseObligationDueInFourthYear" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtProductOrServiceAxis_us-gaapLicenseAndServiceMember_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">10.6</ix:nonFraction> million for the years ending December&#160;31, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Contingencies </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loss contingencies may arise in connection with the ordinary conduct of the Company&#8217;s business activities. The Company considers all loss contingencies on a quarterly basis and based on known facts assesses whether potential losses are considered reasonably possible, probable, and estimable. The Company establishes an accrual for loss contingencies when the loss is both probable and reasonably estimable. If the estimated loss is a range of potential outcomes and there is no better estimate within the range, management accrues the amount at the low end of the range. These accruals represent management&#8217;s estimate of probable losses and, in such cases, there may be an exposure to loss in excess of the amounts accrued. Significant judgment is required to determine both likelihood of there being a probable loss and the estimated amount of a loss. If a loss contingency is not both probable and reasonably estimable, the Company does not establish an accrual, but will evaluate other disclosure requirements and continue to monitor the matter for developments that would make the loss contingency both probable and reasonably estimable. The ultimate outcome of any litigation relating to a loss contingency is uncertain and, regardless of outcome, litigation can have an adverse impact on the Company because of defense costs, negative publicity, diversion of management resources and other factors. </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">109</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In its standard subscription agreements, the Company has agreed to indemnification provisions with respect to certain matters. Further, from time to time, the Company has also assumed indemnification obligations through its acquisition activity. These indemnification provisions can create a liability to the Company if its services do not appropriately calculate taxes due to tax jurisdictions, or if the Company is delinquent in the filing of returns on behalf of its customers. Although the Company&#8217;s agreements have disclaimers of warranties that limit its liability (beyond the amounts the Company agrees to pay pursuant to its indemnification obligations and guarantees, as applicable), a court could determine that such disclaimers and limitations are unenforceable as a matter of law and hold the Company liable for certain errors. Further, in some instances the Company has negotiated agreements with specific customers or assumed agreements in connection with the Company&#8217;s acquisitions that do not limit this liability or disclaim these warranties. It is not possible to reasonably estimate the potential loss under these indemnification arrangements.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</span></p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the offering of the 2026 Notes, the Company purchased capped calls from certain financial institutions with respect to its common stock. The capped calls each have an initial strike price of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001543" name="us-gaap:OptionIndexedToIssuersEquityStrikePrice1" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndTwentySixNotesMember_us-gaapOptionIndexedToIssuersEquityTypeAxis_avlrCappedCallTransactionsMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="2">238.44</ix:nonFraction> per share of the Company&#8217;s common stock, which corresponds to the initial conversion price of the 2026 Notes. The capped calls each have an initial cap price of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001544" name="avlr:InitialCapPrice" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndTwentySixNotesMember_us-gaapOptionIndexedToIssuersEquityTypeAxis_avlrCappedCallTransactionsMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="2">323.30</ix:nonFraction> per share and expire in incremental components on each trading date beginning on June 4, 2026, and ending on July 30, 2026. The capped calls are intended to offset potential dilution to the Company&#8217;s common stock or offset any cash payments the Company is required to make in excess of the principal amount, as the case may be, with such reduction or offset subject to the cap price. The capped calls are subject to adjustments for certain corporate events and standard anti-dilution provisions. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.29%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company paid an aggregate amount of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001545" name="us-gaap:OptionIndexedToIssuersEquitySettlementAlternativesCashAtFairValue" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndTwentySixNotesMember_us-gaapOptionIndexedToIssuersEquityTypeAxis_avlrCappedCallTransactionsMember_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">75.3</ix:nonFraction> million for the capped calls, covering approximately <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001546" name="us-gaap:OptionIndexedToIssuersEquityShares" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndTwentySixNotesMember_us-gaapOptionIndexedToIssuersEquityTypeAxis_avlrCappedCallTransactionsMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">4.1</ix:nonFraction> million shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock. <span style="color:#000000;">As the&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;">capped</span><span style="color:#000000;">&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;">calls</span><span style="color:#000000;"> are both legally detachable and separately exercisable from the 2026 Notes, the Company accounts for the&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;">capped</span><span style="color:#000000;">&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;">call</span><span style="color:#000000;">s separately from the 2026 Notes. The&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;">capped</span><span style="color:#000000;">&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;">call</span><span style="color:#000000;">s are indexed to the Company&#8217;s own common stock and classified in stockholders&#8217; equity. As such, the premiums paid for the&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;">capped</span><span style="color:#000000;">&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;">call</span><span style="color:#000000;">s have been included as a net reduction to&#160;additional paid-in capital&#160;in the consolidated balance sheet.</span>&#160;</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000484" name="us-gaap:DisclosureOfCompensationRelatedCostsShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001348036_20210101_20211231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000484_dcnt_0bec8898-bd3e-47cc-b4d1-59efab8d2678">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">12. Equity Incentive Plans </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has stock-based compensation plans that provide for the award of equity incentives, including stock options, stock awards, RSUs, PSUs, and purchase rights. As of <span style="color:#000000;">December&#160;31, 2021</span>, the Company had stock options outstanding under the 2018 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2018 Plan&#8221;) and the 2006 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2006 Plan&#8221;), RSUs and PSUs outstanding under the 2018 Plan, and purchase rights issued under the ESPP. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The total number of shares of common stock reserved for issuance under the 2018 Plan is equal to (1) <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001568" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandEighteenEquityIncentivePlanMember_20211231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">5,315,780</ix:nonFraction> shares plus (2) any shares subject to outstanding awards under the 2006 Plan as of June 14, 2018 that subsequently cease to be subject to such awards. The available shares automatically increase each January 1, beginning January 1, 2019, by the lesser of (i) <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001569" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardPercentageOfOutstandingStockMaximum" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandEighteenEquityIncentivePlanMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="2" scale="-2">5</ix:nonFraction>% of the aggregate number of shares of common stock outstanding on December 31st of the immediately preceding calendar year (rounded up to the nearest whole share) and (ii) an amount determined by the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors. As of <span style="color:#000000;">December&#160;31, 2021</span>, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001570" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsOutstandingNumber" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandEighteenEquityIncentivePlanMember_20211231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">4,077,218</ix:nonFraction> shares were subject to outstanding awards and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001571" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandEighteenEquityIncentivePlanMember_20211231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">12,042,976</ix:nonFraction> shares were available for issuance under the 2018 Plan. The 2018 Plan provides that on the occurrence of certain strategic events, such as a change in control in which options and RSUs are not assumed or substituted, such outstanding options and RSUs will become fully vested and exercisable or payable. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of <span style="color:#000000;">December&#160;31, 2021</span>, there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001572" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsOutstandingNumber" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandSixEquityIncentivePlanMember_20211231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">1,178,424</ix:nonFraction> shares subject to outstanding stock options under the 2006 Plan.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2019, the Company amended its Outside Director Compensation Policy to modify the vesting provisions for nonemployee director awards in the event of certain terminations of service. The modification resulted in an acceleration of share-based compensation expense for nonemployee director awards in the third quarter of 2019.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Calibri;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Options are granted with an exercise price per share not less than the per share fair market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the grant date. The fair market value per share of the Company&#8217;s common stock for purposes of determining stock-based compensation is the closing price of the Company&#8217;s common stock as reported on the applicable grant date.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Calibri;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Expected volatility for stock options is based on a combination of annualized daily historical volatility of the Company&#8217;s stock price and the historical and implied volatility of comparable publicly traded companies over a similar expected term. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The expected term represents the period that the Company&#8217;s stock-based awards are expected to be outstanding. Given the Company&#8217;s relative inexperience of significant exercise activity, the expected term assumptions were determined based on application of the simplified method of expected term calculation by averaging the contractual life of option grants and the vesting period of such grants. This application, when coupled with the contractual life of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001681" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardExpirationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001348036_20210101_20211231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">ten years</ix:nonNumeric> and average vesting term of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001682" name="avlr:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAverageVestingPeriod" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_avlrEmployeesMember_20210101_20211231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">four years</ix:nonNumeric> for employees and <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001683" name="avlr:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAverageVestingPeriod" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_avlrNonEmployeeDirectorsMember_20210101_20211231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one year</ix:nonNumeric> for non-employee directors, creates an expected term of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001684" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsExpectedTerm1" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_avlrEmployeesMember_20210101_20211231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">six years</ix:nonNumeric> and <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001685" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsExpectedTerm1" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_avlrNonEmployeeDirectorsMember_20210101_20211231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric>, respectively. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has not paid and does not expect to pay dividends. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The risk-free interest rate was based on the rate for a U.S. Treasury zero-coupon issue with a term that closely approximates the expected life of the option grant at the date nearest the option grant date. </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">114</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-size:1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p></td>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the first quarter of 2021, PSUs were granted for the first time. Stock-based compensation cost for PSUs is recognized on a graded vesting basis in the consolidated statements of operations over the period during which the participant is required to perform services in exchange for the award, based on the fair value of the Company&#8217;s underlying common stock on the grant date and the number of PSUs expected to be earned over the service period. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001706" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardTermsOfAward" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20210101_20211231">Each PSU grant will vest in annual tranches over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001707">three-year</span> service period. Total units earned for grants made in 2021 may vary between <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001708" name="avlr:PercentageOfUnitsEarnedOfUnitsGranted" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">0</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001709" name="avlr:PercentageOfUnitsEarnedOfUnitsGranted" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">250</ix:nonFraction>% of the units granted based on the attainment of company-specific performance targets during the related <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001710">three-year</span> period and continued service.</ix:nonNumeric> The performance targets are established by the Compensation and Leadership Development Committee of the Board of Directors. All of the PSUs earned will be settled through the issuance of an equivalent number of shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock based on the payout level achieved.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2021, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001711" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedShareBasedAwardsOtherThanOptions" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">19.9</ix:nonFraction> million of total unrecognized compensation cost related to PSUs was expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of approximately <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001712" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedPeriodForRecognition1" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20210101_20211231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1.9</ix:nonNumeric> years. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employee Stock Purchase Plan </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The ESPP is intended to qualify as an employee stock purchase plan under Section&#160;423 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. Under the ESPP, employee purchases occur at the end of discrete offering periods. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001713" name="avlr:DescriptionOfOfferingPeriodForEmployeeStockPurchasePlan" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20210101_20211231">Offering periods begin on August&#160;1 and February&#160;1 each year (or such other date determined by our Board of Directors or our Compensation and Leadership Development Committee).</ix:nonNumeric> </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">115</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000484_dcnt_1b0e9f7b-8966-4d76-a1e1-43f703810f1a">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the ESPP, eligible employees can acquire shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock by accumulating funds through payroll deductions. Employees generally are eligible to participate in the ESPP if they are a U.S. employee and are employed for at least 20 hours per week. The Company may impose additional restrictions on eligibility. Eligible employees can select a rate of payroll deduction between <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001715" name="avlr:PercentageOfPayrollDeductionOnEligibleCompensation" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">1</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001716" name="avlr:PercentageOfPayrollDeductionOnEligibleCompensation" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">15</ix:nonFraction>% of their compensation. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001717" name="avlr:DescriptionOfPurchasePriceForSharesOfCommonStockPurchasedUnderEmployeeStockPurchasePlan" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20210101_20211231">The purchase price for shares of common stock purchased under the ESPP is <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001718" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardPurchasePriceOfCommonStockPercent" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="2" scale="-2">85</ix:nonFraction>% of the lesser of the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on (i)&#160;the first day of the applicable offering period or (ii)&#160;the last day of the purchase period in the applicable offering period.</ix:nonNumeric> An employee&#8217;s participation automatically ends upon termination of employment for any reason.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company initially reserved <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001719" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20211231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">996,709</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock for sale under the ESPP. The aggregate number of shares reserved for sale under the ESPP increases automatically on each January&#160;1, beginning January&#160;1, 2019, by the number of shares equal to the least of (i)&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001720" name="avlr:IncreaseOfCommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuanceInEachOfCalendarYear" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">1,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock, (ii)&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001721" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardPercentageOfOutstandingStockMaximum" contextRef="C_0001348036_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">1</ix:nonFraction>% of the aggregate number of shares of common stock outstanding on December 31st of the immediately preceding calendar year (rounded up to the nearest whole share), and (iii)&#160;an amount determined by the Board of Directors. No more than an aggregate of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001722" name="avlr:EmployeeStockPurchasePlanNumberOfSharesInitiallyAuthorized" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">10,102,525</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock may be issued over the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001723">ten-year</span> term of the ESPP.<span style="color:#000000;"> As of December&#160;31, 2021</span>, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001724" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20211231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">2,509,441</ix:nonFraction> <span style="color:#000000;">shares of common stock remain available for issuance under the ESPP.</span> </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of <span style="color:#000000;">December&#160;31, 2021</span>, there was approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001725" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedStockOptions" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million of unrecognized stock-based compensation cost related to the ESPP that is expected to be recognized over the remaining term of the offering period that began on August 1, 2021, and ended January 31, 2022. </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000570" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfShareBasedPaymentAwardStockOptionsValuationAssumptionsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_avlrTwoThousandAndEighteenEmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_20210101_20211231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000570_cnt_1">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the TTR and Impendulo acquisitions, the Company recorded net deferred tax liabilities which provide an additional source of taxable income to support the realization of pre-existing deferred tax assets. Accordingly, during the year ended December 31, 2020, the Company released $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001785" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_avlrTTRAndImpenduloAcquisitionsMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">9.5</ix:nonFraction> million of its valuation allowance resulting in a deferred tax benefit for the same amount. Measurement period adjustments made to TTR purchase price accounting during the year ended December 31, 2021, reduced the net deferred tax liabilities recorded to goodwill. As a result, during the year ended December 31, 2021, the Company increased its valuation allowance by $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001786" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_avlrTTRAndImpenduloAcquisitionsMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.9</ix:nonFraction> million resulting in a deferred tax expense for the same amount.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">It is the Company&#8217;s intention to reinvest the earnings of non-U.S. subsidiaries in those operations. As of December&#160;31, 2021, the Company has not made a provision for U.S. or additional foreign withholding taxes for any outside basis differences inherent in its investments in foreign subsidiaries that are indefinitely reinvested. It is not practicable to estimate the amount of deferred tax liability related to investments in these foreign subsidiaries.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The future utilization of federal net operating loss carryforwards generated after 2017 is limited to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001865" name="avlr:NetOperatingLossCarryforwardPercentage" contextRef="C_0001348036_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_us-gaapTaxPeriodAxis_avlrAfterTwoThousandSeventeenMember_20210101_20211231" decimals="2" scale="-2">80</ix:nonFraction>% of taxable income. An additional limitation applies to the use of federal net operating loss and credit carryforwards, under Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, that is applicable if the Company experiences an <span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">&#8220;</span>ownership change<span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">&#8221;</span>. The Company has experienced various <span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">&#8220;</span>ownership changes<span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">&#8221;</span> in prior years. The resulting Section 382 limitations are not expected to materially impact the Company&#8217;s ability to utilize carryforwards. Future changes in the ownership of the Company could further limit the Company&#8217;s ability to utilize its NOLs and credits.</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">118</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000485_dcnt_485ce660-10d9-4e28-85f3-58200142e127">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has assessed its ability to realize its deferred tax assets and has recorded a valuation allowance against such assets to the extent that, based on the weight of all available evidence, it is more likely than not that all or a portion of the deferred tax assets will not be realized. In assessing the likelihood of future realization of its deferred tax assets, the Company placed a significant amount of weight on its history of generating tax losses in the U.S., U.K., and Brazil, including in the current year. The increase in the valuation allowance each period was primarily related to U.S. federal and state tax losses incurred during the period. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has established an accrual for uncertain tax positions related to its U.S. research and development credits and for the valuation of intellectual property transferred between international entities. As of December&#160;31, 2021 and 2020, the Company has $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001866" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="C_0001348036_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">9.1</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001867" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="C_0001348036_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">7.0</ix:nonFraction> million of unrecognized tax benefits, of which the total amount that would impact the effective tax rate, if recognized, is $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001868" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsThatWouldImpactEffectiveTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001348036_20211231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.2</ix:nonFraction> million. As of December 31, 2021, the Company has recorded an immaterial amount of interest and penalties related to its unrecognized tax benefits, which are classified as a component of income tax expense. The Company does not believe it is reasonably possible that its unrecognized tax benefits will significantly change in the next 12 months. </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000576" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfUnrecognizedTaxBenefitsRollForwardTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001348036_20210101_20211231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company files income tax returns in the U.S. federal jurisdiction, and various state and foreign jurisdictions. With limited exceptions, all tax years for which the Company has filed a tax return remain open due to the existence of NOLs. </p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000486" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001348036_20210101_20211231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000486_dcnt_0960edc6-1822-4375-9271-983422241ad8">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">14. Net Loss Per Share Attributable to Common Shareholders </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company calculates basic and diluted net loss per share attributable to common shareholders in conformity with the two-class method required for companies with participating securities. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The diluted net loss per share attributable to common shareholders is computed by giving effect to all potential dilutive common stock equivalents outstanding for the period. This includes using the if-converted method for calculating any potential dilutive effect of the convertible senior notes. For purposes of this calculation, all common stock equivalents have been excluded from the calculation of diluted net loss per share attributable to common shareholders as their effect is antidilutive. As a result, basic and diluted net loss per common share was the same for each period presented. </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000577" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfEarningsPerShareBasicAndDilutedTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001348036_20210101_20211231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000577_dcnt_6ac809b3-816d-4ad7-88c7-bf63b69930c6"></ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_9_CHANGES_IN_DISAGREEMENTS_WITH_ACC">Item 9. Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_9A_CONTROLS_PROCEDURES">Item 9A. Controls and Procedures. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our principal executive officer (Chief Executive Officer) and principal financial officer (Chief Financial Officer), we conducted an evaluation (pursuant to Rule 13a-15(b) of the Exchange Act) of the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures, as defined in Rule&#160;13a-15(e) under the Exchange Act as of <span style="color:#000000;">December&#160;31, 2021</span>.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Disclosure controls and procedures are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in our reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized, and reported, within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and forms. Disclosure controls and procedures include those designed to ensure that such information is accumulated and communicated to management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Based on the evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures as of December&#160;31, 2021, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that, as of such date, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective at the reasonable assurance level.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act). Internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Our internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that: (i)&#160;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of our assets&#59; (ii)&#160;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP, and that our receipts and expenditures are being made only in accordance with authorizations of our management and directors&#59; and (iii)&#160;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of our assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of<span style="color:#000000;"> December&#160;31, 2021</span>, based on the framework in Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) (2013 framework). Based on this evaluation our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that as of<span style="color:#000000;"> December&#160;31, 2021</span>, our internal control over financial reporting was effective. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company acquired INPOSIA Solutions, GmbH on April 1, 2021, <span style="color:#000000;">substantially all the assets of </span><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:Calibri;">DAVO Technologies LLC </span>on April 20, 2021, <span style="color:#000000;">substantially all the assets of </span>3CE Technologies, Inc. on September 7, 2021, <span style="color:#000000;">substantially all the assets of </span>Track1099 LLC on October 1, 2021, and <span style="color:#000000;">substantially all the assets of </span>CrowdReason Limited Liability Company and CorrelationAdvisors LLC on October 18, 2021<span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">. Management excluded these acquisitions from its assessment of the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2021. Total assets excluded from this assessment were $37.6 million, representing 1% of the Company&#8217;s consolidated total assets as of December 31, 2021, total liabilities excluded from this assessment were $33.3 million, representing 2% of the Company&#8217;s consolidated total liabilities as of December 31, 2021, and total revenue excluded from this assessment was $9.6 million, representing 1% of the Company&#8217;s total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2021.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">121</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of </span><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">December&#160;31, 2021</span><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> has been audited by </span><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000036" name="dei:AuditorName" contextRef="C_0001348036_20210101_20211231">Deloitte &#38; Touche, LLP</ix:nonNumeric></span><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in their report which is included in Part II, Item 8, &#8220;Financial Statements&#8221;, of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting in&#160;connection with the evaluation required by Rules&#160;13a-15(d)&#160;and 15d-15(d)&#160;of the Exchange Act that occurred during the three months ended December&#160;31, 2021 that materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Inherent Limitations on Effectiveness of Controls</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management recognizes that a control system, no matter how well conceived and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the control system are met. Further, the design of a control system must reflect the fact that there are resource constraints, and the benefits of controls must be considered relative to their costs. Because of the inherent limitations in all control systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud or error, if any, have been detected. These inherent limitations include the realities that judgments in decision making can be faulty, and that breakdowns can occur because of a simple error or mistake. Additionally, controls can be circumvented by the individual acts of some persons, by collusion of two or more people, or by management override of the controls. The design of any system of controls is based in part upon certain assumptions about the likelihood of future events, and there can be no assurance that any design will succeed in achieving its stated goals under all potential future conditions&#59; over time, controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or the degree of compliance with policies or procedures may deteriorate. Because of the inherent limitations in a cost-effective control system, misstatements due to error or fraud may occur and not be detected.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_9B_OR_INFORMATION">Item 9B. Other Information. </p>

The new employment agreements replace in their entirety those that expired in June 2021 and are materially similar to the prior employment agreements with each of Mr. McFarlane and Ms. Pinney.</p>
